rootCauses.title: <iframe src="javascript:..."> gets no initial about:blank document, so contentWindow.document is null (Akamai mPulse/boomerang loader dies with "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'open')")
rootCauses.area: vendor/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs (load_iframe), crates/script/js/40_webapi.js (iframeWindow/lenient stand-in), crates/engine/src/renderer.rs (frame realm creation, run the javascript: URL)
rootCauses.mechanism: load_iframe (vendor/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:1234-1275) creates the initial blank subdocument only for an empty src or "about:blank" (:1256-1264). A javascript: src falls through to start_iframe_load (:1271-1274), the net provider cannot fetch it and no subdocument is ever attached. iframe.contentWindow then goes L.frameGlobal -> null (crates/script/src/natives/misc.rs:1080 n_frame_global / realm_global :983 return None without a subdoc) and falls back to L.iframeWindow -> remote window stand-in (crates/script/js/40_webapi.js:733). frameIsCrossOrigin (:737) is false for a non-http(s) src, so the stand-in is the 'lenient same-origin child' whose `document` is hard-wired to null (:681) and contentDocument is null (30_html.js:1195/1205). The Akamai mPulse snippet (samsung.com/de inline script, chars ~900-1300) does r=createElement('iframe'); r.src='javascript:void(0)'; insertBefore(...); _=r.contentWindow.document; _.open()._l=...; _.write('<bo'+'dy onload="document._l();">'); _.close() -> TypeError on _.open(), boomerang never loads. In Chromium (and per spec, Ladybird NavigableContainer::create_new_child_navigable / shared_attribute_processing_steps) every iframe starts with a synchronous initial about:blank document; the javascript: URL is evaluated afterwards in it (result undefined => document stays blank). The same TypeError text on theguardian.com (Windows sweep only) is probably the same family (ad/creative loaders that write into a script-created frame) but is NOT reproduced on Linux.
evidence: Repro page probe: variants nosrc/about:blank/srcdoc/empty-src give contentWindow.document 'object'; jsvoid ('javascript:void(0)') and jsvar ('javascript:var d=document.open()...') give document null, contentDocument null, location undefined. Chromium: 'object' for all six.

Minimal repro (iframe-javascript-url.html): Sharko -> {"doc":"null","err2":"TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'open')"}; Chromium -> document object, open() returns the document, write/close OK.

samsung.com/de: extracted the failing inline script (stack 'samsung.com/de/:1:982'): it is the Akamai mPulse boomerang loader with r.src="javascript:void(0)" (go-mpulse.net). Same error in Linux and Windows sweeps.

Even after removing the javascript: src (blank iframe) the full boomerang flow still fails in Sharko: document._l() never runs (see root cause document-write-not-a-parser); with the src both problems stack.

sitediff logs: winsweep/theguardian.com_international/sharko.log:33 same message, stack in an inline script executed inside a frame realm whose URL equals the page URL (src-less/about:blank frames report the parent URL in Sharko: w.location.href of an about:blank iframe is the parent's URL, Chromium 'about:blank').

repro.path: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sharko-browser/8d979774-b495-516b-a198-458f7b9b0b92/scratchpad/rc/script-errors-mixed/repro/iframe-javascript-url.html (sh /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sharko-browser/8d979774-b495-516b-a198-458f7b9b0b92/scratchpad/rc/script-errors-mixed/repro/run.sh iframe-javascript-url); boomerang-snippet.html?js for the full snippet
repro.expected: Chromium: iframe.contentWindow.document is the initial about:blank Document; open()/write()/close() work
repro.actual: Sharko: contentWindow.document === null -> TypeError 'Cannot read properties of null (reading 'open')'

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: high — Akamai mPulse/boomerang RUM snippet is on a very large number of commercial sites (all Akamai customers), and 'javascript:void(0)' / 'javascript:false' hidden iframes are a classic pattern of third-party loaders; the page usually keeps working (analytics silently dead) but the uncaught error aborts the rest of the inline script it sits in.
rootCauses.fixSketch: 1) mutator.rs load_iframe: treat src schemes that never produce a fetchable document (javascript:, and any unsupported scheme) like empty/about:blank: attach the initial blank subdocument (load_iframe_srcdoc(id, "")) and do not call start_iframe_load; remember the javascript: URL. 2) Once the frame realm exists (renderer.rs frame-realm creation, ~1185-1240) queue a task that runs L.runJavascriptURL in the FRAME's realm (today it runs in the parent's, 30_html.js:3004); if the completion value is a string, replace the frame document via document.open/write/close; then fire the iframe's load. 3) Give src-less/about:blank/srcdoc frames the URL 'about:blank' (srcdoc: 'about:srcdoc') for location/document.URL while keeping the parent URL as base URL (blitz uses the parent URL as the subdoc URL, mutator load_iframe_srcdoc/iframe.rs:105-116). 4) Keep the lenient stand-in only as a fallback (documents not created yet), never as the steady state for same-origin frames. Reference: Ladybird LibWeb/HTML/NavigableContainer.cpp (create_new_child_navigable :66, shared_attribute_processing_steps :195-250), Blink LocalFrame initial empty document.

rootCauses.title: document.open()/write()/close() on a script-created or blank document is a body-fragment hack: <html>/<head>/<body> attributes and onload are lost and no load event fires (boomerang's <body onload="document._l()"> never runs; ad-creative iframes lose head/body/html)
rootCauses.area: crates/script/js/90_bootstrap.js (writeInto :784, openWrittenParser :849, docWrite :858, Document.prototype.open/close :892-905), crates/script/js/20_dom.js (parseFragment :1062); a resumable document parser via vendor/blitz-dom / html5ever
rootCauses.mechanism: After parsing, docWrite() clears only the BODY (openWrittenParser -> replaceAllCore(bodyId)) and feeds each written chunk to L.parseFragment with the body as context (writeInto). A fragment parse in body context ignores html/head/body start tags, so <body class onload>, <html lang class>, <head><title>/<meta>/<base>/<style> children are dropped or dumped into the body; the doctype is kept from before. close() only runs the end-queue of written scripts (runEndQueue); it does not move readyState to interactive/complete or fire DOMContentLoaded/load again, and open() never sets readyState to 'loading'. Per HTML, document.open() empties the whole document and creates a script-created parser (Ladybird Document::open -> HTMLParser::create_for_scripting, readiness 'loading'; Blink Document::open/implicitOpen), write() feeds a real tree builder (the 'in body' rule for a <body> start tag merges attributes into the existing body), close() ends the parser and runs the DOMContentLoaded/load steps. Consequence for the mPulse loader: _.open()._l=function..; _.write('<body onload="document._l();">'); _.close() -> body has no onload attribute, no load event -> document._l() never runs -> the boomerang <script> is never appended.
evidence: boomerang-snippet.html (no javascript: src, plain blank iframe, local script URL): Chromium log ['_l ran']; Sharko log [] (no error, callback never runs).

write-body-onload.html: d.open(); d.write('<body onload=...>'); d.close(): Chromium body is <body onload=...></body>, onload ran, readyState complete; Sharko body is <body></body>, onload never ran, readyState 'interactive' right after close().

write-full-document.html: writing 'T

hi

'. Chromium: attributes on html and body kept, title/style in head, onload fired once. Sharko: 'T

hi

' (all attributes lost, head empty, no onload).
Code read: 90_bootstrap.js:849-870 (openWrittenParser clears only body), :784-790 (writeInto = parseFragment in body context), :899-905 (close does not fire load).

repro.expected: Chromium: html/head/body attributes preserved, body onload (window load) fires after close(), readyState 'complete'
repro.actual: Sharko: attributes dropped, head empty, no load event, boomerang callback never runs

sites: samsung.com_de (second stage of the mPulse loader)
rootCauses.estimatedImpact: high — friendly-iframe ad creatives (GPT/AdX/Criteo/Teads), boomerang, sandbox/preview widgets and older loaders all use open/write/close into blank iframes; effects range from lost <body onload> to missing <html class> styling.
rootCauses.fixSketch: Real fix: implement the HTML 'document open steps' with a script-created parser: open() empties the document (doctype, html, head, body), resets readyState to 'loading' and starts a resumable html5ever tokenizer/tree-builder attached to the existing document (blitz already parses documents via html_parser_provider.parse_document; add a streaming variant that keeps the parser alive across write() calls and applies the insertion-mode rules incl. merging attributes of a second <html>/<body> token); write() feeds it; close() ends it, then readyState interactive -> DOMContentLoaded -> complete -> load on the Window (BODY_FORWARDED onload attribute, 10_events.js:773) and the iframe element's load in the parent. Scripts written by write() keep the existing parser-inserted logic (runWrittenScripts). Interim S/M patch inside 90_bootstrap.js: before writeInto, scan the written text for <html ...>/<body ...> start tags and merge their attributes into documentElement/body, hoist leading <title>/<meta>/<base>/<link>/<style> into <head>, and in close() (when reopened) set readyState 'complete' and fire DOMContentLoaded + load via the normal window/body handler path. Reference: Ladybird DOM/Document.cpp (Document::open :1071-1207, close :1220), Blink core/dom/document.cc (Document::open :3817/3983, close :4318).

rootCauses.title: fetch()/XHR (and module/crossorigin subresources) never enforce CORS: a cross-origin response without Access-Control-Allow-Origin is handed to script (Chromium rejects with 'Failed to fetch') — n-tv.de and europa.eu then JSON.parse a WAF/geo-block HTML page
rootCauses.area: crates/netstack (fetch.rs, headers.rs, new preflight cache), crates/common/src/protocol.rs (NetRequest mode/origin), crates/script/js/40_webapi.js (fetch :2492-2560, XHR :2675), crates/script/src/natives/misc.rs (n_fetch :241-300)
rootCauses.mechanism: The JS layer does response tainting only: 40_webapi.js:2513-2545 builds a 'cors'/'opaque'/'basic' Response by comparing origins and filters headers, but nothing looks at Access-Control-Allow-Origin/-Credentials, and there is no preflight (grep 'access-control' finds only the forbidden-header list :1994 and expose-headers :2535). The netstack sends Origin on cross-origin fetch (headers.rs:176) but never checks the answer. So any cross-origin error page (403 geo block, WAF page, CloudFront 'Sorry' page with Retry-After) reaches the page as an ordinary Response. n-tv.de: https://www.lotto24.de/public/product-info/v3/drawinfo/draws is geo-blocked from this sandbox (403 text/html 'block-reason GEO', no ACAO); Chromium: CORS failure -> fetch rejects -> the widget's .catch logs 'TypeError: Failed to fetch'; Sharko: 403 body '<html>\n<head>...' -> .then(e=>e.text()) -> JSON.parse -> 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<', "<html>\n<he"...' (chunk 6842.c04a02b3b7ed8f13.js:1:4619). europa.eu: webtools.europa.eu/rest/wprom returns a cached CloudFront 'Sorry' HTML page with 200 (only for Accept-Encoding gzip/br/zstd variants, no ACAO); Chromium CORS-blocks it, Sharko Response.json() -> SyntaxError (40_webapi.js:2172).
evidence: cors-fetch-xhr.html (page on 127.0.0.1:8765, target http://localhost:8765/json without ACAO): Chromium fetch -> 'TypeError: Failed to fetch', XHR -> onerror; Sharko fetch -> 'OK 200 cors {"a":1}', XHR -> 'OK 200'. Also mode:'no-cors' fetch is sent as mode cors with an Origin header in Sharko (server log) — Chromium sends no Origin and sec-fetch-mode no-cors.
module-headers.html: cross-origin <script type=module src=http://localhost:8765/m2.js> without ACAO: Chromium blocks it ('blocked by CORS policy'), Sharko executes it (window.m2=1).

curl through the proxy with Origin: lotto24 endpoint -> HTTP/2 403 text/html, no ACAO ('<meta name=block-reason content=GEO>'); Chromium on https://www.n-tv.de/ console: 'Access to fetch at lotto24 ... blocked by CORS policy' + 'TypeError: Failed to fetch' (winsweep/n-tv.de/chromium.json errors).

europa.eu: curl with Accept-Encoding 'gzip, deflate, br, zstd' returns 200, 40597 bytes, 'Sorry - 6980483', Retry-After: 5, X-Cache: Hit from cloudfront, no ACAO; without that header the JSON (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). Chromium console: 'Access to fetch at webtools.europa.eu/rest/wprom ... blocked by CORS policy'.
sitediff: n-tv.de Sharko-only 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'' is Chromium's 'TypeError: Failed to fetch' one step earlier; environment (geo/WAF) is the trigger, the missing CORS check is the bug.

repro.expected: Chromium: cross-origin fetch/XHR/module script without a matching Access-Control-Allow-Origin fails (TypeError: Failed to fetch / onerror)
repro.actual: Sharko: the response is delivered and readable

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: medium for site parity (visible only when a server refuses CORS: geo/WAF/error pages, misconfigured APIs, third-party endpoints that 4xx; then error handling paths diverge, sometimes user-visible), high for correctness/security: the same-origin policy is not enforced for script-readable responses.
rootCauses.fixSketch: Put CORS in the network stack so every initiator shares it: extend common NetRequest with mode (cors|no-cors|same-origin|navigate), initiator origin and credentials mode (today only Destination::Fetch/Script/... and `credentials: bool`). In netstack fetch.rs, per hop: (1) no-cors: no Origin on GET/HEAD, opaque response; (2) cors, cross-origin: send Origin, run a preflight (OPTIONS with Access-Control-Request-Method/-Headers, cache keyed by origin+url+credentials with Access-Control-Max-Age) when the method or headers are not CORS-safelisted (port Ladybird Fetch/Fetching/Fetching.cpp http_fetch :1414-1430 and Infrastructure/HTTP/CORS.cpp safelist helpers, Chromium services/network/public/cpp/cors/cors.cc CheckAccess :145); (3) CORS check on the final response and on redirect hops: ACAO equals the serialized origin (or '*' when the request is not credentialed; 'null' rules), ACAC 'true' when credentialed, statuses 304/407 excluded; on failure return a network error (net::ERR_FAILED) and log 'Access to fetch at ... has been blocked by CORS policy: ...' to the console. Then make the JS layer pass real mode/credentials (fetch, XHR, module scripts, <script/link/img crossorigin>, fonts) and delete the tainting-only logic's assumption that any cross-origin response is readable. Keep exemptions for file:, data:, blob:, and same-origin.

rootCauses.title: Script requests carry inverted fetch metadata: classic <script src> = Sec-Fetch-Dest empty/Mode cors (+Origin cross-origin), module scripts = Dest script/Mode no-cors with no Origin, nested imports use the document as Referer; blitz-fetched subresources (css, images, fonts) send no Referer and no Sec-Fetch-Site
rootCauses.area: crates/script/src/modules.rs (start_fetch :355), crates/script/js/90_bootstrap.js (startScriptFetch :417), crates/script/src/natives/misc.rs (n_fetch destination :264), crates/netstack/src/headers.rs (apply_defaults :144, cross_origin_cors :176, apply_sec_fetch :199), crates/netstack/src/provider.rs (BlitzNetProvider::fetch :60 ignores doc_id; to_net_request :143)
rootCauses.mechanism: n_fetch maps everything except mode 'navigate' to Destination::Fetch, so classic scripts (startScriptFetch passes mode no-cors/cors only as a label) go out as Sec-Fetch-Dest: empty, Sec-Fetch-Mode: cors, and cross-origin ones also get an Origin header (headers.rs:176). modules.rs start_fetch uses Destination::Script, so modules get Dest script but Mode no-cors, no Origin, credentials always on, Referer = the document URL even for nested imports. Chromium (captured with a header-logging server): classic = dest script/mode no-cors/no Origin; crossorigin classic and ALL module fetches (also same-origin) = dest script/mode cors + Origin, Referer of a nested import = the importing module; <link rel=modulepreload> is fetched (Sharko never fetches it). Separately BlitzNetProvider::fetch ignores its doc_id argument and blitz Request::get(url) carries no Referer, so stylesheets, images and fonts leave with neither Referer nor Sec-Fetch-Site (apply_sec_fetch derives the site from the referrer).
evidence: module-headers.html + server log. Sharko: /c1.js dest=empty mode=cors; /m1.js and /m1dep.js dest=script mode=no-cors no origin, Referer page.html for the nested import; Chromium: /c1.js dest=script mode=no-cors; /m1.js, /m1dep.js, /pre.js dest=script mode=cors origin=http://127.0.0.1:8765, /m1dep.js Referer=.../m1.js.

subresource-headers.html: Sharko /xs.css and /xs.png: no Referer, no Sec-Fetch-Site; /xs1.js and /xs2.js: dest=empty, mode=cors, Origin present even for the plain classic script. Chromium: xs1.js no Origin, dest script mode no-cors; all with Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site and Referer.
Sharko also sends no Sec-CH-UA / Sec-CH-UA-Mobile / Sec-CH-UA-Platform although the UA claims Chrome/140 (Chromium sends them on every request).

Windows CI: ikea.com/de/de fetched 40x 'Failed to fetch module ...: HTTP 400' (all <script type=module>), dkb.de 1x HTTP 503; the identical 166 module URLs (script tags + modulepreload) return 200 through the sandbox proxy with either Sharko-like or Chromium-like headers (parallel curl, 20 streams), so the header mismatch alone is not shown to cause the 400 — see windows-ci-network-400-503.

repro.path: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sharko-browser/8d979774-b495-516b-a198-458f7b9b0b92/scratchpad/rc/script-errors-mixed/repro/module-headers.html and subresource-headers.html; server request log in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sharko-browser/8d979774-b495-516b-a198-458f7b9b0b92/scratchpad/rc/script-errors-mixed/repro/req.log after sh /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sharko-browser/8d979774-b495-516b-a198-458f7b9b0b92/scratchpad/rc/script-errors-mixed/repro/run.sh module-headers

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: medium — hotlink-protection/Referer allow-lists on image and font CDNs, WAF/bot heuristics keyed on Fetch Metadata or missing Referer/UA-CH, servers that vary on Origin for module scripts; invisible on most sites.
rootCauses.fixSketch: Introduce a request 'mode' next to Destination in NetRequest and derive Sec-Fetch-Mode/Dest from it. Classic script: Destination::Script, no-cors (cors + Origin when the crossorigin attribute is present), credentials per crossorigin; module script and modulepreload: Destination::Script, cors, Origin always, credentials same-origin unless crossorigin=use-credentials, Referer = importing module URL for nested imports (modules.rs start_fetch should take the parent URL; also drop the hard-wired credentials:true of NetRequest::get). BlitzNetProvider: use the doc_id it receives to look up the document URL (renderer registers it per document) and set NetRequest.referrer so Referer/Sec-Fetch-Site are produced by apply_defaults. Add Sec-CH-UA/-Mobile/-Platform (matching the UA string) in apply_defaults, low-entropy set only. Fetch <link rel=modulepreload> as a module fetch.

rootCauses.title: import('blob:...') and <script type=module src=blob:...> fail with net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME
rootCauses.mechanism: modules.rs start_fetch sends every module URL to ScriptHost::fetch -> netstack, which has no blob: scheme. Classic subresource blobs are served by CountingNetProvider (crates/engine/src/host.rs:83+) via script::resolve_blob_url, and fetch()/XHR handle blob: in the JS layer, but the module loader never consults the blob registry.
evidence: module-blob-url.html: Chromium {dyn:'OK 42 dflt', tag:'loaded 1'}; Sharko {dyn:'ERR TypeError: Failed to fetch module blob:http://127.0.0.1:8765/<uuid>: net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME (unsupported scheme `blob:`)', tag:'error'}.

bing.com Linux AND Windows sweeps: 'Uncaught TypeError: Failed to fetch module blob:https://www.bing.com/<uuid>: net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME' (2-3x per load) followed by 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'controller')'.

repro.expected: module loads from the blob URL
repro.actual: TypeError Failed to fetch module blob:... ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: medium — blob-URL modules are used by bundlers, web-worker shims, Bing and various widget loaders.
rootCauses.fixSketch: In modules::start_fetch, for scheme blob: resolve through blob::resolve_blob_url (same registry the JS layer registers into), require the blob URL origin to equal the realm's origin, and complete the fetch on the next task with status 200, content-type = blob type (the existing is_js_mime check then applies) and the bytes; unknown/revoked URL -> the same TypeError as a network error. data: URLs already work through netstack schemes.rs.

rootCauses.title: ikea.com/de and dkb.de: 'Failed to fetch module URL: HTTP 400/503' appears only in the Windows CI sweep (direct connection, no proxy) — CDN/WAF reaction, not reproducible on Linux
rootCauses.area: crates/netstack (HTTP/3 race in fetch.rs send_race :735+, alt_svc.rs; TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint); diagnostics only
rootCauses.mechanism: The 'Failed to fetch module' text is modules.rs:411-412 reporting the status of the module GET; a failed module stays cached as Entry::Failed for the realm (:312, :345) so each <script type=module> for that URL reports the same error. IKEA (Cloudflare; __cf_bm cookies) returned 400 to every module request of the Windows run and also broke 7 images and 21 stylesheets that modules add (Windows probe: 71/92 css links, 6431 rules vs 11394, page 16015px vs 11434 tall, score 73; Linux run score 5 with no module error). dkb.de (MyRA Cloud WAF, x-myracloud) returned 503 to one module — and Chromium in the same Windows run got 503 for 16 resources plus CORS-blocked redirects, so the WAF was blocking the CI address for both browsers. Windows CI differs from the Linux sandbox in three ways that the Linux sweep cannot see: direct connection from an Azure datacenter IP (bot reputation), Sharko's own TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint reaching the origin (through the sandbox proxy all clients share the proxy's fingerprint), and HTTP/3 (h3_allowed :559 is false behind a proxy, so QUIC/Alt-Svc upgrade is only exercised on Windows). None of the request-header differences found (see script-fetch-metadata-parity) reproduce a 400: 166/166 ikea module URLs (script tags + modulepreload) return 200 through the proxy with Sharko-like and Chromium-like headers, in parallel.
evidence: winsweep/ikea.com_de_de/sharko.log: 40 'Failed to fetch module https://www.ikea.com/...: HTTP 400' (30 distinct URLs); Chromium 0 errors; Linux sweep + fresh-profile runs here: no module error.
winsweep/dkb.de/chromium.json: 16x 'Failed to load resource ... 503', 3x ERR_FAILED, CSS blocked via x-myracloud redirect; Sharko: 1x HTTP 503 module.

Local cookies are small (7 cookies, ~1 KB) so a 'cookie too large' 400 is unlikely; Sharko's h2 request on the wire was captured with a local Node h2 server (SHARKO_EXTRA_CA) and is header-for-header identical to curl's.
No synthetic 400 exists in netstack/engine/script (grep).

repro.path: n/a (Windows CI only). Diagnostic run: on Windows `set RUST_LOG=netstack=debug` + `browser --headless --single-process --console --profile=<fresh> --settle=3000 https://www.ikea.com/de/de/` and compare with `set SHARKO_...` http3 off (NetConfig.http3=false).
repro.actual: HTTP 400 for all module GETs from the CI host

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: unknown/low on end-user machines (residential IP), high on CI-style datacenter runs where bot walls decide; ikea's page is badly broken when it happens (modules build the header/listing).
rootCauses.fixSketch: Diagnose first: log for every 4xx/5xx of a Destination::Script request the HTTP version (h2 vs h3), the request header block and the first 200 bytes of the body (the CDN block page names its rule), and rerun the Windows job with HTTP/3 disabled to test the QUIC hypothesis; if it is fingerprint-driven, the fix is impersonation work (Chrome-like ClientHello order/extensions/ALPS, HTTP/2 SETTINGS and pseudo-header order), not per-site. Also worth making failed module fetches non-sticky only if a retry policy is added later (Chromium does cache failures too, so leave as is).

rootCauses.title: sitediff flags uncaught errors as 'Sharko-only' because Chromium's pageerror text lacks the 'TypeError: ' prefix that Sharko's console line has (faz.net's two errors also occur in Chromium)
rootCauses.mechanism: run.js records Chromium uncaught errors as 'Uncaught ' + e.message (Playwright's pageerror message has no error name, e.g. 'Uncaught Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'app')' and 'Uncaught Failed to execute 'define' ... already been used'), while Sharko prints 'Uncaught TypeError: ...' / 'Uncaught NotSupportedError: ...'. signature() does not strip the class name, so the same error on both sides never matches. faz.net: both flagged errors ('NotSupportedError ... dpc-search-widget has already been used' from widget.wc.js executed twice, and 'TypeError ... reading 'app'' from Nuxt's app-manifest timer, _nuxt/CjclePJq.js:1:7185 via setTimeout(getAppManifest,1e3) after window.__NUXT__ is gone) are thrown identically by Chromium (live run: 'Uncaught Failed to execute define...', 'Uncaught Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'app')'; final URL /aktuell/ in both).
evidence: Linux sweep data: of 155 Sharko-only signatures over 74 sites, 16 (10%) become matches once '<Name>Error: ' is stripped on both sides; for coursera.org, cuny.edu, derstandard.at, dict.cc, dwd.de and google.com_search all flagged errors are such artifacts; partial on bing, cloudinary, faz, finn.no, heise, lemonde, rottentomatoes, temu, wetteronline.

Windows sweep: chromium.json for faz.net contains 'Uncaught Failed to execute define ...' and 'Uncaught Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'app')'; samsung.com/de likewise has 'Uncaught Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ECID')' in Chromium vs Sharko '(in promise) TypeError: ...'.
dkb.de: Sharko 'Failed to fetch module ... HTTP 503' vs Chromium 'Failed to load resource ... 503' are the same event with different wording.

repro.expected: same signature on both sides -> not reported
repro.actual: reported as js-errors only in Sharko

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: medium for triage quality: ~10% of the 'Sharko-only error' signatures (and the priority ranking built on them) are false positives.
rootCauses.fixSketch: In run.js normalise both sides: record pageerror as `${e.name}: ${e.message}` (or strip /^(Uncaught )?(\(in promise\) )?\w*(Error|Exception): / in signature()), treat '(in promise)' consistently, and map 'Failed to load resource ... status of N' to the module/subresource wording before comparing.

rootCauses.title: microsoft.com/de-de: Sharko is served Microsoft's 'automated process / request has been blocked' page in the Linux sandbox; the JSON 'Bad control character' error is that page's data-pb attribute, not a JSON decoding difference
rootCauses.area: none in the engine (bot management); possible follow-up: TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint + Sec-CH-UA parity in crates/netstack
rootCauses.mechanism: The document GET returns 200 with a 201 KB 'Your request has been blocked' variant (title 'Your request has been blocked. This could be...', body 'Your current User-Agent string appears to be from an automated process, if this is incorrect, please click this link:'), see out/microsoft.com_de-de/sharko.png. Its shell contains <div class=epb-container data-pb='[{"Browser":..."Title":"Breaking\n   ...'> with a raw LF inside a JSON string at char 567. The shell bundle (UhfPromoBanner constructor, 'define("uhfPromoBanner")', shell/_scrf/js ... ?ver=2.0&iife=1 line 9 col 82827) does JSON.parse(el.getAttribute('data-pb')) whenever #epb exists and no cookie banner blocks it, and the interstitial has no #uhfCookieAlert, so it runs. V8 (node -e JSON.parse on the decoded attribute) throws the identical 'Bad control character in string literal in JSON at position 567 (line 1 column 568)'; Chromium never hits it because it receives the real page (no data-pb attribute at all). Sharko's attribute decoding is correct.
evidence: Sharko headless with fresh profile x3 (single-process, RUST_LOG=netstack=debug): 'GET https://www.microsoft.com/de-de/ -> 200 (HTTP/2, 201253 bytes)', document.title 'Your request has been blocked. This could be due to several reasons.'; Chromium screenshot shows the real page.
Windows CI: Sharko got the real page (title 'Microsoft – AI, Cloud, ...', 541 elements) and no JSON error.

curl through the same proxy: HTTP/1.1 (any headers) -> blocked page; HTTP/2 with Sharko's exact header set (also with Chrome's incl. Sec-CH-UA) -> real page. Sharko's HTTP/2 request captured on the wire (local Node h2 server + SHARKO_EXTRA_CA) equals curl's h2 request header for header (order included: :method :scheme :authority :path, user-agent, accept, accept-language, accept-encoding, upgrade-insecure-requests, sec-fetch-dest/mode/site/user), so the trigger is below the header level (TLS ClientHello / H2 SETTINGS fingerprint or egress behaviour) — not resolved.
node -e "JSON.parse(decoded data-pb)" -> same V8 message; Python json also fails at char 567.

repro.actual: block page in the Linux sandbox; real page on Windows CI

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: low as an engine bug (page-level bot wall); relevant as a reminder that bot walls silently turn sitediff scores into 100 for Akamai/Cloudflare-protected sites (also singular.net shows a block page).
rootCauses.fixSketch: No engine change for the JSON error. sitediff: detect block pages (titles/phrases 'request has been blocked', 'automated process', 'Access Denied') and mark the site 'bot-wall' instead of scoring it. Optional parity work: send Sec-CH-UA* headers, Chrome-like ClientHello/H2 settings.

rootCauses.title: duolingo: 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')' — window.ServiceWorkerRegistration (and navigator.serviceWorker, PushManager, SpeechRecognition) do not exist
rootCauses.mechanism: Duolingo's features-*.js feature detector evaluates "showNotification" in window.ServiceWorkerRegistration.prototype inside try/catch; with ServiceWorkerRegistration undefined it throws, console.error(n) prints it and the feature is recorded as 'no-ServiceWorkerRegistration.showNotification'. window.duo.supportedFeatures in Sharko = [no-CSS Container Query Units, no-PushManager, no-ServiceWorker, no-ServiceWorkerRegistration.showNotification, no-SpeechRecognition, no-webkitSpeechRecognition, no-subgrid]; Chromium = [] (all features present). The page is not blocked by this: the site just disables push prompts and speech exercises. The error itself is caught by the site (console noise only).
evidence: eval on https://www.duolingo.com/: Sharko typeof ServiceWorkerRegistration/navigator.serviceWorker/PushManager/SpeechRecognition/webkitSpeechRecognition = undefined; Chromium function/object; Notification and CompressionStream exist in both.
features-91ec4487.js (line 1 col 613) is the detector array; rest of its checks (BigInt, private fields, dynamic import via data: URL) pass in Sharko.
CSS.supports('(width: 1cqw)') and CSS.supports('grid-template-rows: subgrid') are false in Sharko (Stylo build without container query units/subgrid) — separate CSS item.
rootCauses.estimatedImpact: low — harmless console error; ServiceWorker-family interface objects are checked by many feature detectors, but most guard with 'serviceWorker' in navigator first.
rootCauses.fixSketch: Expose the interface objects ServiceWorkerRegistration, ServiceWorker, ServiceWorkerContainer, PushManager (illegal constructors with the standard prototype members, e.g. showNotification/getNotifications/pushManager) while keeping navigator.serviceWorker absent (sites then skip registration via 'serviceWorker' in navigator). SpeechRecognition stays absent (speech exercises need real recognition). Verify with tools/api-inventory compare.js.
